coordinates.locator: J. Heise, The Sanford Underground Research Facility at Homestake (arXiv:1503.01112), Table 5 Coordinates estimates for various locations of interest, rows LBNF (10 kt Cavern) and LBNF (30 kt Cavern)
coordinates.note: Midpoint of the two LBNF cavern rows of Table 5 in the SURF overview paper (surface-projected positions): LBNF (10 kt Cavern) 44 deg 20 min 45.07 sec N, 103 deg 45 min 17.96 sec W (44.345853, -103.754989) and LBNF (30 kt Cavern) 44 deg 20 min 42.44 sec N, 103 deg 45 min 18.62 sec W (44.345122, -103.755172), about 83 m apart. The PDF text lists the table column by column; the three values in each column follow the order of the three row labels. These are 2015 plan-stage estimates of the LBNF cavern positions, so confidence stays approximate and precision_m is 500. This replaces an earlier OpenStreetMap/Nominatim surface point for the whole site (44.3474397, -103.7548247, about 218 m from the new value; src:surf-osm-nominatim is still listed in the record sources). The DUNE paper and the SURF site establish only that the far detector is at the 4850 ft level at Lead, South Dakota.

notes: Coordinates unresolved to detector precision; see the coordinates note.

summary.plain: Caverns nearly a mile underground at the Sanford laboratory, excavated to hold the huge liquid-argon detectors of the DUNE experiment.
summary.technical: LBNF far-site campus on the 4850-foot level of SURF: two detector caverns and a central utility cavern, about 1500 m of rock (4300 m.w.e.) overburden, hosting the DUNE far detector modules.
